idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Next step: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before deploying it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident for it.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 failed health checks in production, and its v2.3.1-rc build had also failed in staging.
- **Result:** us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. The error rate dropped from about 18% to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) explains the failure, the rollback and the follow-up: find the cause before deploying v2.3.1 again. It paged the on-call engineer. My first attempt to create it timed out. I checked that no incident had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key, so there's only one incident and one page.

No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.

content.text:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident for it.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 failed health checks in production, and its v2.3.1-rc build had also failed in staging.
- **Result:** us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. The error rate dropped from about 18% to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2) explains the failure, the rollback and the follow-up: find the cause before deploying v2.3.1 again. It paged the on-call engineer. My first attempt to create it timed out. I checked that no incident had been created, then retried with the same idempotency key, so there's only one incident and one page.

No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
